*Starts thinking in the farmer's voice...*

---

Aiya, another year. Let me think about what I'm doing on my five mu.

I'm 73 now, been on this land since I was a boy working behind my father. My son works in Shijiazhuang, hasn't come back to farm — only me and the old lady now. Two old people, five mu. It's not much land but these bones aren't what they used to be.

My land is split like always — three mu in cotton on the bigger plot (that's my main crop, been growing cotton there since before my son was born), and two mu near the house where I do wheat in winter and then maize after. The wheat and maize are mostly for us, for flour and for feeding the few chickens. Cotton is what brings money.

**About the cotton.** The hard part is picking. Three mu of cotton means a lot of stooping over from September all the way to November, pick after pick. Last year my back was finishing me by the third pick. My nephew from the next village came for two days to help and I paid him some. This year I'll probably call him again, can't be helped. I buy the same seed I always buy from the agricultural supply shop in town — the shopkeeper Lao Wang has known me 20 years, he gives me the common hybrid everyone in the village uses. I don't try these new fancy Bt varieties the younger farmers talk about, too expensive and I don't trust what I don't know.

For fertilizer on cotton I put down one bag of compound (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu before planting, that's maybe 40 jin, and then when the cotton starts flowering I put some urea, half a bag per mu or so. That's what I've always done. My neighbor Old Liu puts more, he has a bigger farm and more money. I can't afford to copy him, and anyway my cotton does okay — usually 200 jin of lint per mu, sometimes a bit more in a good year.

Bollworms are always a problem on cotton. I spray three, maybe four times through the season. I buy the pesticide from the same shop, the owner tells me which one to use. Doesn't work as well as it used to — the bugs get used to it — but what can you do.

Irrigation on cotton I only do once or twice. The well water costs money to pump and cotton doesn't need as much as maize. If it rains enough in July I might skip it.

**About the wheat.** I plant in mid-October after I've finished the cotton picking around that time (well, the first picks — the last pick can drag on). Wheat is easier on me — you plant it, you water it, you harvest it with the machine the village hires. Same variety as everyone else, Jimai something, the shopkeeper knows. I put down one bag of compound before planting and then topdress with urea in spring when the wheat turns green again, and water it two or three times — once for winter irrigation, once at green-up, once at jointing if the spring is dry. Usually I get about 400 jin per mu from my two mu. That's about 800 jin of wheat — keeps us in flour and some to give to my son's family when they visit.

**About the maize.** Right after wheat harvest in June I plant maize on the same two mu. The turnaround is tight — maybe four or five days. I hire the neighbor with the planter, he does several families' plots in one morning. I buy the hybrid seed (maize you have to buy fresh every year, can't save it). Put down a bag of compound at planting, maybe topdress some urea at the big leaves stage if I see the plants are yellowish. One irrigation if July is dry. Gets me about 450 jin per mu. We eat some, grind some for the chickens, sell a little if there's extra.

I'm not doing anything different this year. What I do works. At my age I'm not going to start trying new things — if it goes wrong I don't have the money to recover. My plan is to keep going like before, Heaven willing.
